question: After train-fixed translation, does a real complementary image improve risk over applying the same two existing models to the anchor image alone?
model_scope: Two models are components of the compared two-forward actions, not optimization replications; no new seed or network training
second_model_translation: Same r019 train-only global integer shift fitting; 256 train regions, four means of fixed pixel BCE, search each coordinate [-32,32], same tie rule and direct check
evaluation: Reuse r018 two-model base probabilities, 128 regions/16 blocks; actual cached labels primary, direct448 labels sensitivity
primary_support: Central384 with train-fixed shifts; zero-shift Central384 descriptive
same_image_action: S_i=(p1701(i)+p1702(i))/2; two forwards and one image
cross_image_action: C_ij12=(p1701(i)+p1702(j))/2; C_ij21=(p1702(i)+p1701(j))/2; two forwards and two images per assignment
assignment_aggregation: Evaluate both pre-fixed model assignments, average their losses; equivalent to uniform assignment selected without labels. Never pool four probabilities or choose better assignment
statistics: Tile mean within block, equal16 blocks; PCG64(17017),20000 paired draws; each co-primary uses two-sided97.5% percentile interval (Bonferroni, approximate bootstrap coverage); 95% descriptive intervals also reported
secondary: Individual assignments, redundancy AU/BV, crossed I, per-action losses and block IoU; assignment IoU ratios first then average
scope: Post-hoc one-pass benchmark; equal model inventory and inference count, different image acquisition requirements; not measured economic cost or all-alternative optimality
